title: Canada's Military Enlists Draganfly for Critical Drone Upgrade
summary: Draganfly Inc. has secured a major contract with the Government of Canada to supply its Low-Cost Tactical ISR UAS to the Canadian Armed Forces. The initial deal includes 100 drone systems, with options for up to 4,900 more, significantly enhancing the military's intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance capabilities.
content:
Calgary-based drone pioneer, Draganfly Inc., has landed a pivotal contract with the Government of Canada, marking a significant stride in modernizing the Canadian Armed Forces' tactical capabilities. The deal sees Draganfly supplying its advanced Low-Cost Tactical ISR Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS), commonly known as drones, for critical intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance missions.

This initial agreement kicks off with an order for 100 of these specialized drone systems, with the potential for the Canadian Armed Forces to acquire an impressive 4,900 additional units over time. The emphasis on 'low-cost' is particularly noteworthy, suggesting a strategic move by the Canadian military to integrate sophisticated yet economically viable solutions into its operational toolkit, maximizing efficiency without compromising on essential ISR functions.

Draganfly, a recognized leader in cutting-edge drone solutions and software, has been at the forefront of transforming various industries with its innovative technology. This contract solidifies their position not just in commercial applications but also as a trusted partner in national defense. Their UAS are designed to provide real-time situational awareness, enhancing decision-making capabilities for ground forces, border patrol, and disaster response scenarios.

The adoption of such advanced drone technology by a national military signals a broader trend in defense strategies worldwide, where agile, autonomous systems are becoming indispensable. For Draganfly, a Canadian company, this represents a substantial boost, showcasing local innovation meeting critical national security needs and potentially opening doors to further international defense collaborations.
keyTakeaways: Draganfly Inc. secured a significant contract to supply Low-Cost Tactical ISR UAS to the Canadian Armed Forces.
The initial order is for 100 drone systems, with options for the Canadian military to acquire up to 4,900 more units.
This partnership enhances Canada's defense capabilities with advanced surveillance technology and boosts Draganfly's position in the defense sector.
author: GlobeNewswire

title: Credit Unions Level Up Estate Management with New DCM Services-AKUVO Alliance
summary: DCM Services and AKUVO have forged a strategic partnership to enhance proactive estate recovery for credit unions, leveraging advanced technology to streamline a sensitive financial process. This collaboration promises greater efficiency and improved compliance, benefiting both institutions and their members during challenging times.
content:
MINNEAPOLIS, Sept. 11, 2026 — In a move set to transform how credit unions manage a particularly sensitive aspect of their operations, DCM Services (DCMS), a recognized leader in estate account resolution, has announced a strategic partnership with AKUVO. The collaboration brings together DCMS’s specialized expertise with AKUVO’s cutting-edge intelligent collections and credit risk platform, promising a more streamlined and proactive approach to estate recovery.

For credit unions, navigating the complexities of estate accounts can be a daunting and emotionally charged task. DCM Services has long stood as the industry benchmark, providing comprehensive solutions that blend compassionate communication with regulatory compliance. Their approach has historically focused on minimizing friction and ensuring respectful interactions during what is often a difficult period for members' families.

AKUVO enters this partnership as a formidable tech innovator, celebrated for its AI-driven platform tailored for financial institutions. Their intelligent system employs advanced analytics and machine learning to optimize collections and mitigate credit risk, offering a level of precision and foresight previously unavailable. Integrating this powerful technological backbone with DCM Services' deep operational knowledge is expected to create a robust ecosystem for managing post-mortem accounts.

The synergy between DCM Services’ human-centric resolution strategies and AKUVO’s data-driven intelligence is poised to redefine proactive estate recovery. Credit unions can anticipate a significant leap in efficiency, with automated processes handling much of the heavy lifting, allowing staff to focus on more complex cases requiring a personal touch. This alliance is not just about recovery; it’s about providing a more thoughtful, transparent, and ultimately more respectful experience for all parties involved, ensuring financial stability while upholding the credit union’s member-first ethos.
keyTakeaways: DCM Services and AKUVO have partnered to enhance proactive estate recovery specifically for credit unions.
The alliance combines DCM Services' human-centric estate resolution expertise with AKUVO's AI-powered intelligent collections and credit risk platform.
This partnership aims to boost efficiency, ensure compliance, and provide a more sensitive and streamlined experience for credit unions and their members during difficult financial times.
author: Staff Writer

title: Neon Giant's NO LAW Dominates Gamescom 2026 with Revolutionary ImSim Promise
summary: At Gamescom 2026, Neon Giant's latest title, NO LAW, emerged as the undeniable standout, promising an immersive simulation experience unlike any other. Moving beyond their previous action-shooter, the studio assures players complete freedom with a 'no wrong way to play' philosophy.
content:
As the dust settles on another electrifying Gamescom, and our comprehensive coverage draws to a close, one game has unequivocally seized the spotlight as my personal highlight of the entire event: NO LAW from Swedish studio Neon Giant. The developers, known for their gritty 2021 isometric twin-stick action shooter, The Ascent, are taking a bold, ambitious leap into new territory.

NO LAW isn't just another title; it's a statement. Shifting gears dramatically from their last outing, Neon Giant is diving headfirst into the immersive simulation (ImSim) genre. This move alone signals a significant evolution for the studio, promising a depth of player agency and environmental interaction that has rarely been seen executed with such confidence.

What truly made NO LAW shine amid a sea of impressive reveals was the developers' unwavering commitment to player freedom. They've explicitly stated that there is “no wrong way to play,” a powerful declaration that hints at complex systems, branching narratives, and unparalleled sandbox potential. This philosophy, central to the ImSim ethos, suggests a game where creative problem-solving and emergent gameplay are not just encouraged, but celebrated.

For a show typically dominated by bombastic trailers and familiar franchises, NO LAW felt like a refreshing, genuinely exciting surprise. It’s a testament to Neon Giant’s evolving vision and their courage to push boundaries. We’re eager to see how this ambitious project, with its promise of limitless possibilities, ultimately redefines player experience when it eventually launches.
keyTakeaways: NO LAW, by Neon Giant, was declared a standout title at Gamescom 2026.
The game marks a significant genre shift for Neon Giant, moving from twin-stick action to an ambitious immersive simulation (ImSim).
Developers emphasize unparalleled player freedom, promising 'no wrong way to play' to encourage creative and emergent gameplay.
author: Alessio Palumbo
